items.quote: If X = {1, 2}, Y {3, 4, 5} Find: X × Y, and represent it:
items.stem: If $X=\{1,2\}$, $Y\{3,4,5\}$ Find: $X\times Y$, and represent it:
solution: The cartesian product of X × Y is represented by an arrow diagram, or a graphical net, as follows:
First: An arrow diagram. Draw an arrow from each element that represents the first projection (the elements of set X) to each element that represents the second projection (the elements of set Y).
i.e: the arrow diagram of the cartesian product represents each ordered pair by an arrow that starts from its first projection and ends at the second projection.

Second: Cartesian diagram (the perpendicular graphical net). On a perpendicular graph net, the elements of set X are represented horizontally and the elements of set Y vertically. The intersection points of the horizontal and vertical lines represent the ordered pairs of the elements of the cartesian product X × Y.
items.notes: Example begins at the bottom of the page; its solution continues on the next page. A circled 1 marks the first item.

items.quote: X Y 1 2 3 4 5 X × Y
items.caption: Arrow diagram for X × Y: left oval X containing 1 and 2, right oval Y containing 3, 4, 5. Arrows from 1 to 3, 4, 5 and from 2 to 3, 4, 5 (six arrows). Labelled X × Y below.

Cartesian diagram (perpendicular graphical net) for X × Y: X = 1, 2 along the horizontal axis (bottom), Y = 3, 4, 5 along the vertical axis (left). Grid intersection points marked and labelled (1,3), (2,3), (1,4), (2,4), (1,5), (2,5). Labelled X × Y.
items.notes: Axis labels 'X' at top left and 'Y' at bottom right as printed; verify.

items.quote: If X = {3, 4 , 8} then find, X × X and represent it
items.stem: If $X = \{3, 4, 8\}$ then find $X \times X$ and represent it with an arrow diagram.
solution: Notice in the figure: the ordered pairs are represented by arrows, and the ordered pairs in which the first projection is equal to the second projection as: (3,3), (4,4), (8,8) are represented by a buttonhole to show that the arrow comes from a point and ends in the same point.

In this case, the cartesian product X × X can be represented graphically by 9 points where each point represents an ordered pair. But if X is an infinite set then the number of elements of X×X is infinite.
items.notes: Answer is the product set; arrow diagram is the figure.

items.notes: Arrow directions read from figure; verify.
